metadata.label: Contact section visibility
metadata.name: ClientConfig.applicantExperience.contact
metadata.description: Reusable Site contact policy. Hide the whole business/employer section regardless of selected products, and independently hide the correspondence destination question. WAEPA uses both flags; other Sites retain their template defaults.
metadata.usedIn: Contact rendering, field collection and validation
metadata.defaultValue: Business address and correspondence use standard template behavior
metadata.options: hideBusinessAddress: true/false; hideCorrespondence: true/false. Optional businessAddressProducts explicitly limits business collection to selected product keys and takes precedence over hideBusinessAddress. Omitted flags default to false.

metadata.label: Custom icons
metadata.name: ClientConfig.branding.icons
metadata.description: Optional client artwork for QuickDecision and coverage categories (LI, AD, DI, OO, SH). Shared icons remain the fallback when an override is absent or cannot load.
metadata.usedIn: QuickDecision, category headers, selectors, quote tools, coverage, beneficiary and payment
metadata.options: Optional quickDecision asset and categories keyed by LI, AD, DI, OO, SH; omitted assets use standard icons

metadata.label: Single-page artwork display
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.singlePageArtwork
metadata.description: Single-page only: defaults to hero text with no decorative images. Opt into the animated clouds, cat and umbrella together. The primary cloud sits above the 800px hero; artwork uses the primary theme palette, is hidden from assistive technology and pauses for reduced motion. Multi-page ignores this setting.
metadata.options: none (default); clouds-cat-umbrella (single-page only)

metadata.label: Homepage applying-steps presentation
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.applyingStepsPresentation
metadata.description: Client selects regular images (default) or the animated application preview, independently of homepage variant. Welcome-back hides the section; drawer explanations remain static and reduced-motion preferences pause animation.
metadata.options: image (default); animated

metadata.label: TPA lookup and decision policy
metadata.name: ClientConfig.tpaIntegration
metadata.description: Standard / AMA: First Name, Last Name and DOB; existing members with active coverage use simulated identity verification. Pass enables portfolio and auto-approval; fail/skipped/no active coverage goes to TPA admin manual review. ASCE additionally matches Membership ID and state, then collects the full residential address before opening member verification. WAEPA: new member auto-approves, existing member goes to manual review; neither runs identity verification nor shows a portfolio. Prototype records simulate API responses.
metadata.defaultValue: Standard coverage verification: First Name, Last Name, DOB; manual review unless matched with active coverage and identity passed
metadata.options: mode: coverage-verification or membership-auto-approval; lookupFields: field IDs (ASCE adds member-id and state-province); requireAddressBeforeVerification: collect the residential address before member verification; prototypeRecords: facts and activeCoverage boolean

metadata.label: Client branding
metadata.name: ClientConfig.branding
metadata.description: Client name, short acronym, logo asset, and logo alt text. If the logo fails to load, the client name is displayed instead.
metadata.options: name; acronym; logo asset path; logo alt text; optional icons.quickDecision asset path

metadata.label: Site theme
metadata.name: ClientConfig.theme
metadata.description: Sets one theme color and an optional filled-primary-button color override, plus standard or pill button shape. Links, controls and supporting accents use the theme color. Other palette roles use the shared template defaults.
metadata.options: Preset: default, teal, purple, dark-blue; or one custom primary color. Optional primaryAction: { main: hex, tone: light or dark } overrides filled primary buttons; otherwise buttons inherit the theme color. buttonShape: pill (default) or standard.

metadata.label: Applicant labels
metadata.name: ClientConfig.applicantLabels
metadata.description: Overrides the default Member/Spouse/Child headings across Coverage and applicant sections. Max 20 characters. Does not affect applicant IDs or business logic.
metadata.options: member, spouse, child — custom text up to 20 characters each

metadata.label: Support phone & hours
metadata.name: ClientConfig.support.phone / phoneDisplay / phoneHours
metadata.description: Machine-readable support phone, human-readable display version, and optional support hours. When configured, the help banner renders 'Call for help' with optional hours.
metadata.options: phone; phoneDisplay; optional phoneHours — free-form text

metadata.label: Support email, website & address
metadata.name: ClientConfig.support.email / website / address
metadata.description: Support email, client website (full URL or bare domain), and structured mailing address. Each is hidden when absent.
metadata.options: email; website URL/domain; address: organization, street, city, state, ZIP

metadata.label: License disclosures
metadata.name: ClientConfig.licenseInfo[]
metadata.description: Array of client licensing disclosure strings shown in the footer or legal area. Rendered in configured order.
metadata.options: Zero or more disclosure strings, in display order

metadata.label: Hide email contact box
metadata.name: ClientConfig.emailSupport.hideContactBox
metadata.description: When true, suppresses the "Questions? We're here to help" contact box in this client's outbound emails (autosave, pending/deletion reminders, submission confirmation, and the advisor-sent application email).
metadata.usedIn: Email Templates (Global/Client tabs), outbound mock emails
metadata.options: Show contact box; Hide contact box

metadata.label: Email support override
metadata.name: ClientConfig.emailSupport.supportOverride
metadata.description: Overrides the client-configured phone, email, and website shown in the emails' support box. Unset properties fall back individually to ClientConfig.support.
metadata.usedIn: Email Templates (Global/Client tabs), outbound mock emails
metadata.options: phone; email; website — each optional and independently inherited

metadata.label: Email contact override
metadata.name: ClientConfig.emailSupport.contactOverride
metadata.description: Overrides the client-configured name and acronym used for the contact shown in the emails' support box. Unset properties fall back individually to ClientConfig.branding.
metadata.usedIn: Email Templates (Global/Client tabs), outbound mock emails
metadata.options: name; acronym — each optional and independently inherited

metadata.label: Landing Page variant
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.homePageVariant
metadata.description: Selects the homepage layout independently of applying-step presentation. Welcome-back hides the applying-steps section; other variants use the separate image/animated setting.
metadata.options: default; quoteFirst; hero-image; welcome-back (steps hidden)

metadata.label: Default form template
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.defaultTemplate
metadata.description: Selects the client's default form layout. The compact layout forces the app into its narrow responsive presentation and places Membership directly after the Home hero. Overrideable per session by the ?template= URL parameter.
metadata.options: single; multi

metadata.label: Support banner chat
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.chat / chatUrl
metadata.description: Enables chat in the shared support banner across portal pages. chatUrl sets the support destination; disabling chat hides the banner action.
metadata.options: Disabled; Enabled with a valid chat URL

metadata.label: Schedule-a-call support
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.scheduleUrl
metadata.description: Displays a 'Schedule a call' action in the help banner, opening a scheduling page in a modal.
metadata.options: None; valid scheduling URL

metadata.label: Custom help/action link
metadata.name: ClientConfig.features.linkUrl / linkLabel
metadata.description: Optional client-defined action link (URL + label) in the help banner. Not displayed when absent or without a valid destination.
metadata.options: None; valid URL with a custom label

metadata.label: Beneficiary & Payment page mode
metadata.name: ClientConfig.pages.requirements.beneficiary / payment
metadata.description: Controls whether Beneficiary and Payment participate in the application flow. Excluded pages are removed from routing, the stepper, breadcrumbs, and Review; non-required pages begin with a Yes/No prompt. The older pages.excluded and pages.optional arrays are deprecated.
metadata.options: required; optional; none

metadata.label: Category label overrides & expand behavior
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverages.categorySectionLabels / allCategoriesExpanded
metadata.description: Per-category display label overrides and a boolean controlling whether category accordions start expanded on load.
metadata.options: Labels for LI, AD, DI, OO, SH; accordions collapsed or expanded

metadata.label: Coverage amount basis
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverages.additionalCoverageWarning
metadata.description: Controls whether applicants enter an additional amount or a total coverage amount.
metadata.options: applyForAdditional; applyForTotal

metadata.label: Enabled products & overrides
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverages.enabled / overrides
metadata.description: Selects the products offered by the site and applies per-product presentation, eligibility, identifier, underwriting, and supporting-content overrides.
metadata.options: Products: li-term, li-10yr, li-15yr, li-20yr, li-50plus, li-add, li-preferred, li-premier-accident, li-group-term, di-ltd-plus, di-ltd, di-mtd, di-step-rated, di-level-rated, di-short-term, oo-professional, oo-office-overhead, sh-critical-illness, sh-hospital-money, sh-hospital-income. Overrides: name, brochure URL, category (LI/AD/DI/OO/SH), identifiers, situs, riders, waiting/benefit periods, applicants (member/spouse/child), notes, featured, underwriting (FUW/GI/NA/QD/SI/TELE), warning, structured content

metadata.label: Scoped coverage amounts
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverages.coverageAmounts[productId]
metadata.description: Defines the coverage amounts available for each product and applicant scope, including derived dependent coverage.
metadata.options: Selection: range (min/max/increment), amount list, or labeled option list; scope: all, member, spouse, child, or applicant class; dependent calculation: percentage or fixed

metadata.label: Waiting period & benefit period options
metadata.name: overrides[].waitingPeriodOptions / maxBenefitPeriodOptions
metadata.description: Defines the elimination/waiting periods and maximum benefit periods offered for applicable DI/OO products.
metadata.options: Waiting period: label, value, days; maximum benefit period: label, value; optionally scoped to member, spouse, or child

metadata.label: Rider definitions
metadata.name: overrides[].riders
metadata.description: Defines the riders offered per product and their pricing and health-routing behavior. Rider IDs must be stable across config changes.
metadata.options: id; name; description; optional amount selections; applicants (member/spouse/child); premium factor

metadata.label: Frequency toggle
metadata.name: ClientConfig.estimatedRateDisplay
metadata.description: Controls the monthly/annual frequency toggle and default frequency for estimated cost display.
metadata.options: Frequency toggle: shown or hidden; default frequency: monthly or annual

metadata.label: Cost breakdown & supplemental fees
metadata.name: productEstimatedCostBreakdown / policyFee / childApplicantRider
metadata.description: Controls supplemental cost line items beneath product estimates.
metadata.options: Breakdown enabled or disabled; policy fee label + monthly/annual amount; child rider enabled or disabled + label + monthly/annual amount

metadata.label: Coverage question section rules
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverageQuestions
metadata.description: Controls which Coverage page question sections appear: always-shown sections, removed default sections, and per-category additional sections. References stable section IDs from the shared pageSections catalog.
metadata.defaultValue: Shared default personal, work/income, and business question sections
metadata.options: Always-show or remove-default section IDs; per-category additions for LI, AD, DI, OO, SH

metadata.label: Hide smoker/nicotine question (quote tool)
metadata.name: ClientConfig.coverages.hideSmokerQuestion
metadata.description: When true, filters smoker/nicotine-use fields from the canonical category-question requirements used by QuoteCalculator. It does not redefine which coverage categories require smoker data.
metadata.defaultValue: No — show smoker/nicotine question when applicable
metadata.options: Show smoker/nicotine question; Hide smoker/nicotine question

metadata.label: Per-page field overrides
metadata.name: ClientConfig.fields[pageId].extra / hidden / required / overrides
metadata.description: Controls field presence, requirement, and presentation per client and page. Hidden fields must not be required, and field IDs must exist in the catalog.
metadata.options: Per page: extra, hidden, or required registered field IDs; overrides for label, placeholder, helper text, and options

metadata.label: Additional membership fields
metadata.name: ClientConfig.fields.membership.extra
metadata.description: Additional Membership fields resolved from the same scoped field catalog used by the application: ASCE Membership ID; AMA physician information for spouse applicants; WAEPA new-member qualification and associated-member fields. Conditional display is governed by the linked field visibility rules.
metadata.usedIn: Membership page and field visibility rules
metadata.options: Registered Membership field IDs with Client/Site scope and optional visibility conditions

metadata.label: Notices and additional fields
metadata.name: ClientConfig.reviewPolicy
metadata.description: Ordered Review blocks with source references, applicant/product/mode applicability and canonical field IDs. Acknowledgement and identity inputs use standard field components with configurable required status before Next. Fraud notices vary by residence and coverage. Assigned medical-authorization guards follow participation in the configured health-question pages; processing-only QD status does not trigger authorization.
metadata.defaultValue: State-specific MCR fraud notices; no additional Review blocks
metadata.options: Ordered blocks with canonical field IDs, paragraphs, optional unordered lists, after-list content and source references; applicant/product/mode/association/jurisdiction predicates; conditional consent; actual-health-question participation guard for medical authorization and its introductory statement; source wording variants by jurisdiction and underwriting; optional point-size and before-signature placement; jurisdiction fraud text and Site overrides

metadata.label: Mutually exclusive products
metadata.name: overrides[].requirements.exclusiveProducts
metadata.description: Product keys that cannot coexist anywhere in the application. Enforced during selection and validation.
metadata.options: Array of enabled product keys that cannot coexist across applicants

metadata.label: Rate input participation
metadata.name: overrides[].rateInputs
metadata.description: Product pricing dimensions: required, ignored or provisional. Includes gender, tobacco, age, jurisdiction, applicant, amount, periods, association, riders and client-specific rate classes. Fixed quote assumptions and tobacco-based class mappings are separate from field visibility. Independent from page field visibility; persisted reviewed policies retain source references and assumption authority.
metadata.defaultValue: No authored rate input override; candidate policy must be captured explicitly
metadata.options: version 1; dimensions required / ignored / provisional; authority source / provisional; source references; jurisdiction dimension/class overrides; rateClass catalog with single / fixed / tobacco / unresolved selection

metadata.description: Whether the estimated cost total box exposes a rate-table link/action.
Whether product cards link to their related rate table.
Presentation type for the linked rate table; product/site relationship resolves actual asset.

FRAUD NOTICE:  Any person who knowingly and with intent to defraud any insurance company or other person files an application for insurance or statement of claim containing any materially false information or conceals for the purpose of misleading, information concerning any fact material thereto commits a fraudulent insurance act, which may be a crime and may subject such person to criminal and civil penalties.  Any insurance company or agent who defrauds or attempts to defraud an insured shall be reported to the Colorado Division of Insurance within the Department of Regulatory Agencies.

FRAUD NOTICE: For your protection California law requires the following to appear on this form.

Any person who knowingly presents false or fraudulent information to obtain or amend insurance coverage or to make a claim for the payment of a loss is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in state prison.

FRAUD NOTICE:  Any person who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or knowingly presents false information in an application for insurance is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in prison.

FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or knowingly presents false information in an application for insurance is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in prison.

FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly or willfully presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or who knowingly or willfully presents false information in an application for insurance is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in prison.

FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: It is a crime to provide false or misleading information to an insurer for the purpose of defrauding the insurer or any other person. Penalties include imprisonment and/or fines. In addition, an insurer may deny insurance benefits, if false information materially related to a claim was provided by the applicant.

FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly and with intent to injure, defraud, or deceive any insurer files a statement of claim or an application containing any false, incomplete, or misleading information is guilty of a felony of the third degree.

FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or knowingly presents false information in an application for insurance may be guilty of insurance fraud as determined by a court of law.

FRAUD NOTICE: It is a crime to knowingly provide false, incomplete, or misleading information to an insurance company for the purpose of defrauding the company. Penalties may include imprisonment, fines or a denial of insurance benefits.
FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: Any person who includes any false or misleading information on an application for an insurance policy is subject to criminal and civil penalties.

FRAUD NOTICE: For accident and health insurance only, any person who knowingly and with intent to defraud any insurance company or any other person files an application for insurance or statement of claim containing any materially false information, or conceals for the purpose of misleading, information concerning any fact material thereto, commits a fraudulent insurance act, which is a crime, and shall also be subject to civil penalty not to exceed five thousand dollars and the stated value of the claim for each such violation.

FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: Any person who knowingly, and with intent to injure, defraud or deceive any insurer, makes any claim for the proceeds of an insurance policy containing any false, incomplete or misleading information is guilty of a felony.

FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who, knowingly and with the intent to defraud, presents false information in an insurance request form, or who presents, helps or has presented a fraudulent claim for the payment of a loss or other benefit, or presents more than one claim for the same damage or loss, will incur a felony, and upon conviction will be penalized for each violation with a fine no less than five thousand (5,000) dollars nor more than ten thousand (10,000) dollars, or imprisonment for a fixed term of three (3) years, or both penalties. value.title: How your Assignment of Dividends to ABE works - The Unique Charitable Giving Feature of ABE-Sponsored Insurance
paragraphs: Founded by the ABA in 1942, the American Bar Endowment (ABE) is a §501(c)(3) not-for-profit public charity. ABE fulfills its charitable mission of improving the administration of justice, one of the profession's highest obligations, by making annual grants to support law-related research, public service, and educational projects and programs, including those conducted by the American Bar Association's Fund for Justice and Education (FJE) and the American Bar Foundation (ABF). ABE also makes Opportunity Grants to support boots-on-the-ground efforts to expand the availability of legal services to underserved communities. ABE maintains a Legal Legacy Fund for the support of its grantees.

By participating in ABE's group insurance programs, designed for and available only to practicing lawyers and their families, you can contribute to these efforts. By enrolling in ABE-sponsored insurance programs, unless you notify the ABE otherwise pursuant to the procedures set forth below, you agree to donate to ABE your share of any dividends payable on the group policies for ABE to use for its charitable purposes. Donations of dividends to ABE are tax-deductible to the insured to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Your dividend donation to ABE makes a difference. These funds, after administrative expenses, are the primary source of ABE's charitable grants and additions to the Legal Legacy Fund. Insureds who donate their dividends help meet their professional and public responsibilities, as well as obtain valuable coverage for their families. About 83% of insured lawyers donate their dividends.

Insureds are notified each year by late January of the amount, if any, of their dividend for the prior year that has been donated to ABE. (Dividends are not guaranteed, and in any given year, a given policy may not pay a dividend; dividends will vary from year to year.)

If you do not want to donate your dividend to ABE, you must request a “refund” of your dividend as follows: any time after the first policy year of your participation, for each year that you want a refund of your dividend, ABE must receive a written request from you for refund (by mail or email to dividends@abendowment.org), by as early as January 1 but not later than December 15 of the year for which a refund is requested. ABE will send confirmation of any request received, and you should retain that confirmation for your records as proof that your refund request was timely received. If you do not receive a confirmation within 3 weeks of sending a request to ABE, please contact the ABE. (Special instructions for new applicants are contained in the application and apply to any dividends earned during the first policy year only). The approximate percentage of premium available for refund (if any) on each ABE-sponsored insurance policy will be published in each December/January issue of the ABA Journal and on ABE's website each October. You do not need to wait for this information as refund requests are accepted beginning January 1.

Donation acknowledgments of your dividend, or dividend checks (if applicable), are mailed by late January the following year. If you receive a donation acknowledgment but you did not intend to donate your dividend to ABE, you may request a one-time waiver of the December 15 deadline by asking for a refund, if you have not previously requested such a waiver.

Please note: Insureds who do not want to contribute dividends to ABE must make a written request for refund each year, using the procedures above. When you sign the application for insurance, you are agreeing to donate your dividends unless you otherwise notify the ABE to request a refund. Do not sign the application if you do not agree with these procedures.

DIVIDEND:
I further understand and agree that any dividend apportioned to the group policy may be retained by the American Bar Endowment to support its charitable mission supporting law-related education, research, and public service projects and programs unless such dividends are claimed by me (or the certificate owner) pursuant to the procedures described in the plan brochures, on the back of the ABE premium notices, and in the plan description material on the ABE website. (Notice of the approximate percentage of premium available, if any, for contribution or refund will be published in the December/January issue of the ABA Journal and on ABE’s website in October.) The Internal Revenue Service has ruled that members who donate their dividends to ABE are eligible for a charitable contribution deduction on their individual income tax returns to the fullest extent permitted by law.

byJurisdiction.MD: FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly or willfully presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or who knowingly or willfully presents false information in an application for insurance is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in prison.
byJurisdiction.DC: FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: It is a crime to provide false or misleading information to an insurer for the purpose of defrauding the insurer or any other person. byJurisdiction.FL: FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly and with intent to injure, defraud, or deceive any insurer files a statement of claim or an application containing any false, incomplete, or misleading information is guilty of a felony of the third degree.
byJurisdiction.KS: FRAUD NOTICE: Any person who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim for payment of a loss or benefit or knowingly presents false information in an application for insurance may be guilty of insurance fraud as determined by a court of law.
byJurisdiction.ME: FRAUD NOTICE: It is a crime to knowingly provide false, incomplete, or misleading information to an insurance company for the purpose of defrauding the company. Penalties may include imprisonment, fines or a denial of insurance benefits.
byJurisdiction.NJ: FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: Any person who includes any false or misleading information on an application for an insurance policy is subject to criminal and civil penalties.
byJurisdiction.NY: FRAUD NOTICE: For accident and health insurance only, any person who knowingly and with intent to defraud any insurance company or any other person files an application for insurance or statement of claim containing any materially false information, or conceals for the purpose of misleading, information concerning any fact material thereto, commits a fraudulent insurance act, which is a crime, and shall also be subject to civil penalty not to exceed five thousand dollars and the stated value of the claim for each such violation.
byJurisdiction.OK: FRAUD NOTICE - WARNING: Any person who knowingly, and with intent to injure, defraud or deceive any insurer, makes any claim for the proceeds of an insurance policy containing any false, incomplete or misleading information is guilty of a felony.

blocks.title: How your Assignment of Dividends to ABE works - The Unique Charitable Giving Feature of ABE-Sponsored Insurance
paragraphs: Founded by the ABA in 1942, the American Bar Endowment (ABE) is a §501(c)(3) not-for-profit public charity. ABE fulfills its charitable mission of improving the administration of justice, one of the profession's highest obligations, by making annual grants to support law-related research, public service, and educational projects and programs, including those conducted by the American Bar Association's Fund for Justice and Education (FJE) and the American Bar Foundation (ABF). ABE also makes Opportunity Grants to support boots-on-the-ground efforts to expand the availability of legal services to underserved communities. ABE maintains a Legal Legacy Fund for the support of its grantees.

By participating in ABE's group insurance programs, designed for and available only to practicing lawyers and their families, you can contribute to these efforts. By enrolling in ABE-sponsored insurance programs, unless you notify the ABE otherwise pursuant to the procedures set forth below, you agree to donate to ABE your share of any dividends payable on the group policies for ABE to use for its charitable purposes. Donations of dividends to ABE are tax-deductible to the insured to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Your dividend donation to ABE makes a difference. These funds, after administrative expenses, are the primary source of ABE's charitable grants and additions to the Legal Legacy Fund. Insureds who donate their dividends help meet their professional and public responsibilities, as well as obtain valuable coverage for their families. About 83% of insured lawyers donate their dividends.

Insureds are notified each year by late January of the amount, if any, of their dividend for the prior year that has been donated to ABE. (Dividends are not guaranteed, and in any given year, a given policy may not pay a dividend; dividends will vary from year to year.)

If you do not want to donate your dividend to ABE, you must request a “refund” of your dividend as follows: any time after the first policy year of your participation, for each year that you want a refund of your dividend, ABE must receive a written request from you for refund (by mail or email to dividends@abendowment.org), by as early as January 1 but not later than December 15 of the year for which a refund is requested. ABE will send confirmation of any request received, and you should retain that confirmation for your records as proof that your refund request was timely received. If you do not receive a confirmation within 3 weeks of sending a request to ABE, please contact the ABE. (Special instructions for new applicants are contained in the application and apply to any dividends earned during the first policy year only). The approximate percentage of premium available for refund (if any) on each ABE-sponsored insurance policy will be published in each December/January issue of the ABA Journal and on ABE's website each October. You do not need to wait for this information as refund requests are accepted beginning January 1.

Donation acknowledgments of your dividend, or dividend checks (if applicable), are mailed by late January the following year. If you receive a donation acknowledgment but you did not intend to donate your dividend to ABE, you may request a one-time waiver of the December 15 deadline by asking for a refund, if you have not previously requested such a waiver.

Please note: Insureds who do not want to contribute dividends to ABE must make a written request for refund each year, using the procedures above. When you sign the application for insurance, you are agreeing to donate your dividends unless you otherwise notify the ABE to request a refund. Do not sign the application if you do not agree with these procedures.

DIVIDEND:
I further understand and agree that any dividend apportioned to the group policy may be retained by the American Bar Endowment to support its charitable mission supporting law-related education, research, and public service projects and programs unless such dividends are claimed by me (or the certificate owner) pursuant to the procedures described in the plan brochures, on the back of the ABE premium notices, and in the plan description material on the ABE website. (Notice of the approximate percentage of premium available, if any, for contribution or refund will be published in the December/January issue of the ABA Journal and on ABE’s website in October.) The Internal Revenue Service has ruled that members who donate their dividends to ABE are eligible for a charitable contribution deduction on their individual income tax returns to the fullest extent permitted by law.

However, members Members who do not want to contribute these dividends are required to "opt out" each year, using the procedures described below. By signing this application, you are agreeing to make an annual decision whether to opt out. Do not sign the application if you do not agree with these procedures.

For the first policy year only,* if you want to opt out, sign and date the initial election below. Written requests may be sent by mail, fax, or email to dividends@abendowment.org. You will be sent a confirmation; retain this for your records. If it is not received within 3 weeks, contact ABE promptly to obtain another.

wording.defaultText:
AUTHORIZATION:  
I authorize any licensed physician, medical practitioner, hospital, pharmacy, clinic or other medical or medically related facility, laboratory, insurance company, MIB, LLC. ("MIB"), or other organization, institution or person, that has any records or knowledge of me or my health to release information, including prescription drug records, maintained by physicians, pharmacy benefit managers, and other sources of information to New York Life Insurance Company, its reinsurers, its subsidiaries or the plan administrator about the physical and mental health of any persons proposed for insurance, including significant history, findings, diagnosis and treatment, but excluding psychotherapy notes for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. Health information obtained will not be re-disclosed without my authorization unless permitted by law, in which case it may not be protected under federal privacy rules. For example, New York Life may be required to provide it to insurance, regulatory, or other government agencies. In this case, the information may no longer be protected by the rules governing your AUTHORIZATION.

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original. In all circumstances, my authorized agent, representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life Insurance Company. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

 “Bloodborne pathogen” means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  hepatitis  B  virus  (HBV),  hepatitis  C  virus  (HCV),  and  human  immunodeficiency  virus  (HIV).  

“Emergency medical services person” means an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergencymedical  services  such  as  a  firefighter,  paramedic,  emergency  medical  technician,  licensed  nurse,  rescue  squad  person,  or  other  individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally  recognized  by  a  political  subdivision  in  the  state,  who  provides  out-of-hospital  emergency  medical  services  during  theperformance of the individual’s duties, an individual employed as a licensed peace officer, a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in criminal investigation, an individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency, or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a good Samaritan, and any individual who, in the process of executing a citizens’ arrest, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.

AUTHORIZATION:  I authorize physicians, practitioners, hospitals, clinics or medically related facilities, pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, laboratories, insurance companies, MIB, LLC (“MIB”), medical information retrieval services, electronic health record companies or health care information technology companies to  release to New York Life Insurance Company or New York Life Insurance and Annuity Corporation (collectively “New York Life”), its reinsurers, or the plan administrator at New York Life’s expense, whether in electronic or paper form, information they may have about my physical or mental health, my prescription drug history, diagnostic testing  and copies of my drug and alcohol records, including my records relating to substance abuse education, prevention, training, treatment, rehabilitation or research. This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

•	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). •	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice. •	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). The information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may become subject to further disclosure.
•	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

AUTHORIZATION:  I authorize physicians, practitioners, hospitals, clinics or medically related facilities, pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, laboratories, insurance companies, MIB, LLC (“MIB”), medical information retrieval services, electronic health record companies or health care information technology companies to  release to New York Life Insurance Company or New York Life Insurance and Annuity Corporation (collectively “New York Life”), its reinsurers, or the plan administrator at New York Life’s expense, whether in electronic or paper form, information they may have about my physical or mental health, my prescription drug history, diagnostic testing  and copies of my drug and alcohol records, including my records relating to substance abuse education, prevention, training, treatment, rehabilitation or research. This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

I understand and agree that:
•	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). The information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may become subject to further disclosure.
•	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

As used in the Statement of Health the medical questions above:

 “Bloodborne pathogen” means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  hepatitis  B  virus  (HBV),  hepatitis  C  virus  (HCV),  and  human  immunodeficiency  virus  (HIV).  

“Emergency medical services person” means an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergencymedical  services  such  as  a  firefighter,  paramedic,  emergency  medical  technician,  licensed  nurse,  rescue  squad  person,  or  other  individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally  recognized  by  a  political  subdivision  in  the  state,  who  provides  out-of-hospital  emergency  medical  services  during  theperformance of the individual’s duties, an individual employed as a licensed peace officer, a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in criminal investigation, an individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency, or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a good Samaritan, and any individual who, in the process of executing a citizens’ arrest, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.

 “Source individual” means an individual, living or dead, whose blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids may be a source of bloodborne  pathogen  exposure  to  an  emergency  medical  service  person.  Examples  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  a  victim  of  an  accident, injury, or illness, or a deceased person.

"Significant exposure” means contact likely to transmit a bloodborne pathogen, in a manner supported by the most current guidelines and recommendations of the United States Public Health Service at the time an evaluation takes place, that includes: (1) percutaneous injury,  contact  of  mucous  membrane  or  nonintact  skin,  or  prolonged  contact  of  intact  skin;  and  (2)  contact,  in  a  manner  that  may transmit a bloodborne pathogen, with blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids.

wording.defaultText:
AUTHORIZATION:  
I authorize any licensed physician, medical practitioner, hospital, pharmacy, clinic or other medical or medically related facility, laboratory, insurance company, MIB, LLC. ("MIB"), or other organization, institution or person, that has any records or knowledge of me or my health to release information, including prescription drug records, maintained by physicians, pharmacy benefit managers, and other sources of information to New York Life Insurance Company, its reinsurers, its subsidiaries or the plan administrator about the physical and mental health of any persons proposed for insurance, including significant history, findings, diagnosis and treatment, but excluding psychotherapy notes for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. Health information obtained will not be re-disclosed without my authorization unless permitted by law, in which case it may not be protected under federal privacy rules. For example, New York Life may be required to provide it to insurance, regulatory, or other government agencies. In this case, the information may no longer be protected by the rules governing your AUTHORIZATION.

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original. In all circumstances, my authorized agent, representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life Insurance Company. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

As used in the Statement of Health the medical questions above:

 “Bloodborne pathogen” means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  hepatitis  B  virus  (HBV),  hepatitis  C  virus  (HCV),  and  human  immunodeficiency  virus  (HIV).  

“Emergency medical services person” means an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergencymedical  services  such  as  a  firefighter,  paramedic,  emergency  medical  technician,  licensed  nurse,  rescue  squad  person,  or  other  individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally  recognized  by  a  political  subdivision  in  the  state,  who  provides  out-of-hospital  emergency  medical  services  during  theperformance of the individual’s duties, an individual employed as a licensed peace officer, a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in criminal investigation, an individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency, or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a good Samaritan, and any individual who, in the process of executing a citizens’ arrest, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.

 “Source individual” means an individual, living or dead, whose blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids may be a source of bloodborne  pathogen  exposure  to  an  emergency  medical  service  person.  Examples  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  a  victim  of  an  accident, injury, or illness, or a deceased person.

"Significant exposure” means contact likely to transmit a bloodborne pathogen, in a manner supported by the most current guidelines and recommendations of the United States Public Health Service at the time an evaluation takes place, that includes: (1) percutaneous injury,  contact  of  mucous  membrane  or  nonintact  skin,  or  prolonged  contact  of  intact  skin;  and  (2)  contact,  in  a  manner  that  may transmit a bloodborne pathogen, with blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids.

AUTHORIZATION:  I authorize physicians, practitioners, hospitals, clinics or medically related facilities, pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, laboratories, insurance companies, MIB, LLC (“MIB”), medical information retrieval services, electronic health record companies or health care information technology companies to  release to New York Life Insurance Company or New York Life Insurance and Annuity Corporation (collectively “New York Life”), its reinsurers, or the plan administrator at New York Life’s expense, whether in electronic or paper form, information they may have about my physical or mental health, my prescription drug history, diagnostic testing  and copies of my drug and alcohol records, including my records relating to substance abuse education, prevention, training, treatment, rehabilitation or research. This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

I understand and agree that:
•	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). The information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may become subject to further disclosure.
•	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me.

This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

I understand and agree that:
•	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). The information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may become subject to further disclosure.
•	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

 “Bloodborne pathogen” means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  hepatitis  B  virus  (HBV),  hepatitis  C  virus  (HCV),  and  human  immunodeficiency  virus  (HIV).  

“Emergency medical services person” means an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergencymedical  services  such  as  a  firefighter,  paramedic,  emergency  medical  technician,  licensed  nurse,  rescue  squad  person,  or  other  individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally  recognized  by  a  political  subdivision  in  the  state,  who  provides  out-of-hospital  emergency  medical  services  during  theperformance of the individual’s duties, an individual employed as a licensed peace officer, a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in criminal investigation, an individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency, or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a good Samaritan, and any individual who, in the process of executing a citizens’ arrest, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.

 “Source individual” means an individual, living or dead, whose blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids may be a source of bloodborne  pathogen  exposure  to  an  emergency  medical  service  person.  Examples  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  a  victim  of  an  accident, injury, or illness, or a deceased person.

"Significant exposure” means contact likely to transmit a bloodborne pathogen, in a manner supported by the most current guidelines and recommendations of the United States Public Health Service at the time an evaluation takes place, that includes: (1) percutaneous injury,  contact  of  mucous  membrane  or  nonintact  skin,  or  prolonged  contact  of  intact  skin;  and  (2)  contact,  in  a  manner  that  may transmit a bloodborne pathogen, with blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids.

value.title: ABE dividend information
value.text:
Founded by the ABA in 1942, the American Bar Endowment is a §501(c) (3) not-for-profit organization composed of members of the American Bar Association. ABE fulfills its charitable purpose of improving the administration of justice, one of our profession’s highest obligations, by making annual grants to support legal research, public service and educational projects in the field of law, including those conducted by ABA’s Fund for Justice and Education (FJE) and the American Bar Foundation (ABF). ABE also maintains a Legal Legacy Fund for the permanent support of its grantees. By participating in the Endowment's group insurance programs, designed for and available only to ABA members, members can contribute to these efforts.Members who enroll in ABE-sponsored insurance programs agree that their share of any dividends payable on the group policies may be retained by ABE for its charitable purposes unless reclaimed as outlined below. The Internal Revenue Service has ruled that members who donate their dividends to ABE are eligible for a charitable contribution deduction on their individual income tax returns. Contributions to ABE are tax deductible under Section 170(c) of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, in accordance with IRS regulations and the March 1987 ruling provided to ABE by the IRS.

Members who donate dividends to ABE make a difference. These funds, after administrative expenses, are the primary source of ABE's charitable grants and additions to the Legal Legacy Fund. Insured members who donate their dividends help meet their professional and public responsibilities, as well as obtaining valuable coverage for their families. About 85% of members donate their dividends; these members are notified each year by late January of the amount, if any, of their dividend donation for the prior year. (Dividends are not guaranteed, and in any given year, a given plan may not pay a dividend; dividends will vary from year to year.)

Members who wish to request a refund of their dividends may do so. The approximate percentage of premium available for refund (if any) on each plan will be published in each November issue of the ABA Journal. You do not need to wait for this information as refund requests are accepted beginning January 1. To request that dividends be paid to you rather than donated to ABE: After the first policy year of your participation, a written request for refund (by mail, fax, or email to dividends@abendowment.org) must be made each year and must reach the Endowment by December 15. When ABE receives your refund request, it will send a confirmation. Retain this for your records as proof your request was timely received. If you do not receive a confirmation within 3 weeks, contact the ABE promptly to obtain another copy. (Special instructions for new applicants are contained in the application and apply to dividends, if any, during the first policy year only.)

Dividend checks and/or contribution notices for your tax return are mailed by late January. If you receive a contribution notice and you did not intend to make a contribution, you may request a one-time waiver of the December 15 deadline by asking for a refund, if you have not previously requested such a waiver.

Please note: Members who do not want to contribute dividends to ABE must make a written request for refund each year, using the procedures above. When members sign the application, they are agreeing to make an annual decision whether to contribute. Do not sign the application if you do not agree with these procedures.
